adds.title: Ministry of the Interior confirmation December 2021 on transgender marriage
adds.summary: Under Estonia's Family Law Act as clarified in December 2021, a marriage validly entered into between a man and a woman remains valid and is not automatically invalidated if one spouse later changes sex even though same-sex marriage was not then permitted, annulment requires a court decision on application by a spouse or in the public interest with the Minister of the Interior having a discretionary right but no obligation to apply for annulment on public interest grounds and each case assessed individually, with Justice Ministry guidance that after societal changes in the previous five to six years same-sex marriage could no longer be said to be contrary to Estonian public order and fewer than 10 marriages in Estonia having become same-sex marriages as a result of gender reassignment of one spouse.

adds.title: Constitution of Fiji (2013), Article 26(3)
adds.summary: Under Fiji's 2013 Constitution Article 26(3), unfair direct or indirect discrimination on grounds including sex, gender, sexual orientation, and gender identity and expression is prohibited.
